Population increased in Birmingham

The estimated population of Birmingham in 2024 was 1,183,618 usual residents, a rise of 1.1% since 2023.

This meant that Birmingham's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Birmingham increased by 3.5%.

Over this slightly longer period, Birmingham was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Birmingham

The average (median) age fell to 33.7 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Birmingham has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Birmingham is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Birmingham's population of 1,183,618 usual residents was made up of:

  • 259,195 people aged 0 to 15 years, (21.9%)
  • 770,017 people aged 16 to 64 years, (65.1%)
  • 154,406 people aged 65 years and over, (13%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Birmingham has a lower proportion of people aged 65 years and over (13% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Birmingham, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Birmingham
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Birmingham, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 5,583 people (0.5%). In total, there were 14,598 births and 9,015 deaths in Birmingham.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 16,373 (-1.4%). There were 63,236 people entering the area and 79,609 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Birmingham's population of 24,235 (2.1%) as a result of 38,707 people entering the area and 14,472 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Birmingham was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Birmingham in mid-2023 is 1,170,238.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 2,481 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 1,708 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 4,189 people.
